claims.text: Pack cementation aluminization of a Mo-Nb-Ta-W refractory high-entropy alloy will introduce aluminum at its surface.
The aluminization treatment will form a continuous, thin, adherent Al2O3 scale on the alloy surface.
Aluminum introduced by pack cementation will diffuse to the surface.
The surface aluminum will react with oxygen to form alumina.
The resulting alumina scale will be slow-growing and thermodynamically stable.
The alumina scale will impede oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Impeded oxygen diffusion will reduce the oxidation rate of the aluminized alloy.
After exposure at 1100°C in dry air containing 21% O2 for 100 hours, the aluminized alloy will have approximately 4–5 times lower mass gain than the untreated alloy.
The untreated Mo-Nb-Ta-W refractory high-entropy alloy will exhibit greater mass gain and more extensive oxidation than the treated alloy.
The predicted benefit is confined to oxidation at 1100°C in dry air for 100 hours and may not hold at other temperatures, oxygen pressures, or exposure times.
The magnitude of oxidation improvement will depend on optimization of the pack composition and processing parameters.
Excessive aluminum diffusion may alter the alloy's bulk properties.
